title: Hyperdescent for the generated total-site topology
statement: Let $I$ be a small poset and let $i\mapsto\mathcal C_i$ be a strict covariant diagram of small Grothendieck sites [def-weil-size-convention], with transition functors $\iota_{ij}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ that are full-sieve inclusions (full, and with every arrow whose target is in the image having source in the image). The topology on $\mathcal C_i$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal C_j$ for $i\le j$: covering sieves on an object of $\mathcal C_i$ are identical in the two categories, since every arrow into it has source in $\mathcal C_i$. Here a Grothendieck topology means covering sieves containing the maximal sieve and closed under pullback and transitivity, and a family covers if its generated sieve covers. No fibre products in the categories are assumed. Form $\mathcal E$ with objects $(i,T)$, $T\in\mathcal C_i$, and arrows $(i,T)\to(j,S)$ for $i\le j$ given by arrows $\iota_{ij}T\to S$ in $\mathcal C_j$. Assume the local lower-refinement condition: for $i,j\le k$, $T\in\mathcal C_i$, $S\in\mathcal C_j$, and an arrow $S\to T$ in $\mathcal C_k$, there is a covering family $\{S_\alpha\to S\}$ in $\mathcal C_j$ and indices $l_\alpha\le i,j$ such that each $S_\alpha$ is in the image of $\mathcal C_{l_\alpha}\to\mathcal C_j$. Give $\mathcal E$ the topology generated by vertical covering families and singleton identity-underlying transition arrows $(i,T)\to(j,\iota_{ij}T)$. Let $\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ be the enhanced derived category of complexes of modules over a commutative ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones, lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal, lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison, lem-coef-projective-cochain-monoidal-model]. A coherent presheaf means an enhanced functor $F:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf D(\Lambda)$ with the higher naturality data of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For each $i$, write $F_i$ for the restriction of $F$ to the fibre $\mathcal C_i$, and call the maps $F(j,\iota_{ij}T)\to F(i,T)$ induced by the singleton transition arrows the transition restriction maps. A hypercover of an object $(i,T)$ in $\mathcal E$ means an augmented simplicial family of representable presheaves whose degree-$n$ map to the presheaf of compatible proper faces (to $h_{(i,T)}$ in degree zero) is an epimorphism after set-sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]; matching presheaves are finite limits in presheaves, and evaluation of $F$ on a family is the product of its values. Then, for every fixed integer $a$, such an $F$ is a hypersheaf (for every hypercover $U_\bullet\to(i,T)$ its descent map $F(i,T)\to\operatorname{holim}_{[n]\in\Delta}F(U_n)$ is an equivalence) and has $H^r(F(i,T))=0$ for $r<a$ if and only if each fibre presheaf $F_i$ is a hypersheaf on $\mathcal C_i$ with the same pointwise lower bound and all transition restriction maps are equivalences. This equivalence is natural under restriction to subposets for which the restricted diagram satisfies the same local lower-refinement condition (in particular, lower-closed subposets).

source.place: Opening compactification step; no supplied source proves the mixed-cover hyperdescent argument. WANTED: a hyperdescent theorem for a Grothendieck construction with local lower refinements.

proof.text: Use the presheaf matching formulation of hypercovers in the statement. A degree-$n$ matching section is a finite compatible collection of proper faces: the nondegenerate proper faces of $\Delta^n$ are finite, and every lower-dimensional operator factors through a face followed by degeneracies. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact], forming these finite matching limits commutes with sheafification. By [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts], the matching map is epic after sheafification exactly when every such presheaf matching section locally lifts on a covering sieve. Thus it suffices throughout to test actual finite matching boundaries on test objects; no matching object in the original category is asserted to exist.

proof.text: For a sieve $R$ on $(j,S)$ define its shadow $\overline R$ on $S$ in $\mathcal C_j$ by declaring $u:V\to S$ to belong when there are $i\le j$, $V\in\mathcal C_i$, and the arrow $(i,V)\xrightarrow{u}(j,S)$ in $R$. If $W\to V$ is an arrow in $\mathcal C_j$, the full-sieve property puts $W$ in $\mathcal C_i$ and lifts this arrow there; closure of $R$ under precomposition therefore puts $W\to S$ in $\overline R$. Hence the shadow is a sieve. The shadow of the maximal sieve is maximal, and taking shadows preserves inclusions. All witness families are small by [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Declare $R$ to be a shadow cover when $\overline R$ covers in $\mathcal C_j$. Check pullback along $h:(b,B)\to(j,S)$, with underlying map $v:B\to S$. The covering sieve $v^*\overline R$ is a sieve in $\mathcal C_b$ by the full-sieve and restricted-topology hypotheses. For $w:W\to B$ in it choose a witness $(i,W)\to(j,S)$ in $R$. Apply the lower-refinement condition to $W\in\mathcal C_i$, $W\in\mathcal C_b$ and its identity in $\mathcal C_j$: it gives a $\mathcal C_b$-cover $W_\alpha\to W$ with labels $l_\alpha\le i,b$. The arrows $(l_\alpha,W_\alpha)\to(b,B)$ lie in $h^*R$, since their composites factor through the chosen witness in $R$. Thus $w^*\overline{h^*R}$ covers for every $w\in v^*\overline R$; transitivity in $\mathcal C_b$ proves that $\overline{h^*R}$ covers.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Check transitivity for shadow covers. Suppose $R$ is a shadow cover of $(j,S)$ and $Q$ is a sieve such that $h^*Q$ is a shadow cover for every arrow $h$ in $R$. An arrow $u:V\to S$ in $\overline R$ has a witness $h:(i,V)\to(j,S)$ in $R$. The cover $\overline{h^*Q}$ of $V$ in $\mathcal C_i$ is also a cover in $\mathcal C_j$ by the restricted-topology hypothesis, and every one of its arrows, after composition with $u$, belongs to $\overline Q$. Consequently $u^*\overline Q$ covers for every $u\in\overline R$, so transitivity in $\mathcal C_j$ makes $\overline Q$ covering. Together with the maximal-sieve and pullback checks this defines a Grothendieck topology.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Every generating vertical cover is a shadow cover because its shadow contains its original covering sieve. For a generating transition $t:(i,T)\to(j,T)$, every arrow $V\to T$ of $\mathcal C_j$ has $V\in\mathcal C_i$ by the full-sieve property, and the corresponding $(i,V)\to(j,T)$ factors through $t$. Its shadow is therefore maximal. Hence the topology generated in the statement is contained in the shadow topology.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Conversely, if $\overline R$ covers $S$, take the covering family of all its arrows $u:V\to S$ and choose a witness $h_u:(i_u,V)\to(j,S)$ in $R$ for each. The vertical arrows $(j,V)\to(j,S)$ form a generating cover. Each is preceded by the generating singleton transition $(i_u,V)\to(j,V)$; transitivity of the generated topology says their composites $h_u$ cover. Since $R$ contains them, it covers. Thus a total sieve covers exactly when its shadow covers in the target fibre. The argument includes the empty covering family.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: The lower-refinement condition also supplies a simultaneous lower label for any finite boundary over a test object $W$ of $\mathcal C_k$. Suppose the boundary pieces have labels $i_1,\ldots,i_m\le k$ and maps from $W$ to their underlying objects in $\mathcal C_k$. The full-sieve property places $W$ in every $\mathcal C_{i_t}$. Induct on $m$: for $m=0$ use the identity cover with label $k$. Given a covering with labels $r\le k,i_1,\ldots,i_{m-1}$, apply lower refinement to the identity of each of its domains, viewed in $\mathcal C_r$ and $\mathcal C_{i_m}$ inside $\mathcal C_k$. The resulting covers in $\mathcal C_r$ remain covers in $\mathcal C_k$; their composites cover $W$ and have labels $l\le r,i_m$. For each boundary piece $(i_t,T_t)$ the underlying map from a refined domain $W_\alpha$ defines an arrow $(l,W_\alpha)\to(i_t,T_t)$: both objects are in $\mathcal C_{i_t}$, so fullness supplies the underlying arrow there. The boundary compatibility equations hold in each required fibre by faithfulness into $\mathcal C_k$. No single lower bound for infinitely many labels is used.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Let $U_\bullet\to(k,S)$ be a total hypercover. On the slice over $(k,S)$ define $r_k(i,T\to S)=T\to S$ in $\mathcal C_k$, and let $V_\bullet$ be the same simplicial family with all objects and arrows sent by $r_k$. For a degree-$n$ matching section of $V_\bullet$ on $W\in\mathcal C_k$, the preceding finite-boundary argument gives a cover $W_\beta\to W$ and labels $l_\beta$ on which it lifts to a matching section of $U_\bullet$ on $(l_\beta,W_\beta)$. The local lifting criterion [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts] supplies a covering sieve of total arrows lifting that matching section to $U_n$. By the shadow-cover characterization its underlying arrows form a cover in $\mathcal C_{l_\beta}$, and hence in $\mathcal C_k$. Their composites with $W_\beta\to W$ give local lifts to $V_n$. Applying the same criterion on $\mathcal C_k$ proves that $V_\bullet\to S$ is a hypercover. For $n=0$ the boundary has no pieces, so the identity cover with label $k$ starts the argument.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Assume the fibre hypersheaf and transition-equivalence conditions. The arrows $z=(i,T\to S)\to(k,r_kz)$ are natural in the total slice: for $(i,T)\to(j,T')$, the two composites to $(k,T')$ have the same underlying arrow by strict functoriality of the diagram. Applying $F$ produces a coherent transformation from the augmented diagram of $F_k(V_\bullet)$ to that of $F(U_\bullet)$, with equivalence components. For each family take products; their universal property carries componentwise equivalences to equivalences. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] this is an equivalence of coherent diagrams. It identifies the limiting cones and their augmentation maps. Since $V_\bullet\to S$ is a fibre hypercover, the given fibre descent map $F_k(S)\to\operatorname{holim}_\Delta F_k(V_n)$ is an equivalence, and so is the original total descent map. This proves total hyperdescent directly for every hypercover.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: For the converse, a fibre hypercover $V_\bullet\to S$ in $\mathcal C_k$ is a total hypercover after putting label $k$ on every piece. Indeed a total test object $(i,W)$ mapping to a matching boundary has $i\le k$. Forgetting its label gives a matching boundary in $\mathcal C_k$, whose local lifts form a covering sieve there by [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts]. Every domain of this sieve belongs to $\mathcal C_i$ by the full-sieve condition on $W$, and the same sieve covers in $\mathcal C_i$ by topology restriction. The corresponding vertical cover of $(i,W)$ gives the required total lifts. Thus total hyperdescent evaluates to exactly fibre hyperdescent.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Each transition $t:(i,T)\to(j,T)$ is a monomorphism of the total category: maps into its source with equal composites have the same label and the same underlying map, hence are equal. Its constant augmented simplicial family, with one copy of $(i,T)$ in every degree and all operators identities, is a hypercover of $(j,T)$. In degree zero the covering singleton gives the local lifting sieve for every arrow into $(j,T)$, so its sheafification is epic by [lem-cbc-presheaf-sheafification-epi-local-lifts]; in degree one a matching section on any test object is a pair of maps to $(i,T)$ with equal composites to $(j,T)$, so monicity makes the two maps equal. In every higher degree, the compatible faces are determined by their vertex maps, all equal by the degree-one check; conversely that single map gives all the faces. Thus every positive matching map is an isomorphism of presheaves.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: Total hyperdescent for the preceding constant hypercover gives $F(j,T)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{\Delta}\operatorname{const}Y$, with $Y=F(i,T)$. The category $\Delta$ is nonempty and filtered: its terminal object $[0]$ is a common successor for every pair of objects and coequalizes every parallel pair. By the filtered-category clause of [lem-cbc-cofiltered-coherent-equivalence-diagrams], the constant functor $\mathscr D\to\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(N(\Delta),\mathscr D)$, with $\mathscr D=\mathbf D(\Lambda)$, is an equivalence. Its full faithfulness identifies $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr D}(X,Y)$ with the mapping space from $\operatorname{const}X$ to $\operatorname{const}Y$ for every $X$; fullness of the equivalence-arrow subcategory identifies the latter with the same mapping space in all coherent diagrams. These are the maps induced by the constant identity cone. The cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] therefore says that this specific cone with apex $Y$ is limiting. Its degree-zero projection is the identity, so the degree-zero projection from any limit is an equivalence. Composing that projection with the hyperdescent equivalence gives exactly the transition restriction $F(j,T)\to F(i,T)$, which is consequently an equivalence.

source.place: Agent proof of the total-site hyperdescent foundation

proof.text: The pointwise lower bound on the total presheaf and the common lower bound on its fibres are literally the same inequalities, since every object is a pair $(i,T)$. For a subposet satisfying local lower refinement, restriction retains fibre hyperdescent, all transition equivalences and the same bound. The implication already proved makes the restricted presheaf a hypersheaf for its own generated topology. Both descriptions use the same values and restriction maps, so the equivalence of conditions commutes with this restriction. If the subposet is lower-closed, every lower-refinement label already lies in it. This proves exactly the qualified naturality assertion.

Step 12: Delta is filtered with terminal [0]; the filtered clause of the cofiltered lemma plus the cone criterion make the identity cone limiting, and the degree-0 projection of the descent cone is F(t).
